beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Limits of Machine Intelligence asks what a machine can justify before its next action.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A check can cover ten steps without settling every possible future.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This exploratory book connects mathematical limits with the permissions we give working systems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You learn to separate a useful guarantee from an unsupported extension.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine a small controller whose counter can increase at each step.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Our teaching example checks every modeled path through its first ten steps.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: No forbidden state appears within that horizon, so the bounded check succeeds.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An eleventh step can cross the limit that the original question excluded.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book distinguishes that precise local result from a promise about unlimited operation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A counterexample can refute a safety claim with one concrete execution.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Proving wider safety needs more than a longer collection of successful runs.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Now change the controller so its counter cannot increase beyond ten.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book compares proofs of such limits with tests and observations during operation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its AI example separates proposing a code change, testing it, and deploying it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A model may suggest freely while execution remains inside a restricted sandbox.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Deployment requires its own stronger check or human authorization.
